protocol.hypothesis: Do the first 10 PCs of PGC hidden activity support better goal/movement readout, and lose less readout accuracy relative to all 256 PCs?
targets: Remembered pickup x,y (not physical goal center)
protocol.selection: Same 3392 known-goal states for both targets and all models; the one unknown-goal state is excluded.
protocol.method: Linear ridge readouts of PCA prefixes. 4 whole-episode outer folds and 3 whole-episode inner folds. PCA, centering, and a scalar feature scale are fitted on each training fold only. No neuron/PC rescaling or whitening.
protocol.alpha_selection: Inner validation mean squared coordinate error, separately for each PC count and target.
protocol.full_anchor: Fresh 256-PC readout on identical samples/alpha grid. Equivalent to ridge on all h; do not substitute the earlier full readout with its smaller alpha grid.
protocol.compression_penalty: Error using 10 PCs minus error using 256 PCs. Lower means less loss when restricted to leading PCs. Negative values are allowed: finite-sample PCA denoising can improve generalization.
protocol.statistics: Four primary contrasts: two targets times 10-PC error/compression penalty. Two-sided paired t and exhaustive sign-flip across 8 seeds, Holm corrected within these 4 contrasts separately per method. Pointwise t CIs are not simultaneous. Other PC counts are descriptive.
protocol.limitations: Exploratory linear decodability on one scripted replay; goal code is externally supplied, movement/facing/vision are correlated. A result cannot establish causal use, recurrent attractors, gridness, or why reward improves. No new policy rollouts or model training.
